newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico urged to go on with econ, political reform.
newsitem.headline: Mexico urged to go on with econ, political reform.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker has urged Mexico to continue with political reforms but said the main priority should be to move forward with economic transformation.

"Continuing economic reform is still substantial for sustained growth in Mexico and the rest of Latin America," he told the State of the World Forum, a gathering of former world leaders in this central Mexican city, late on Thursday.
Baker said Latin American nations should carry out more privatisation of state assets and drop exchange rates and price controls.
Mexico has moved to an open economy in the past decade, culminating in 1994 with entry into the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) with the United States and Canada.
Baker, secretary of state under President George Bush, said Mexico's second priority was political reform and increased democracy, but it would not be an easy transition.

He said President Ernesto Zedillo's efforts at political reform had been partly thwarted by certain sectors of his own ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). "Unfortunately this attempt was put back owing to the forces of opposition inside his own party. This is a shame and we would like to see this (democratic) progress continue," he said.

PRI legislators recently watered down political reforms aimed at fairer elections. Last-minute changes to a reform bill included restricting coalitions of opposition parties and scrapping a special body to audit party finances.

In a videotaped message to the three-day forum, Zedillo said Mexico could not be pressured by foreign countries to change at a faster rate. "Democracy cannot be transplanted from one society to another nor can it be imposed by foreign pressures or interferences ... democracy develops in each country in accordance with its own political evolution."
